key_insight: Learned diffusion proposals help constraint solving only in a narrow regime; for many continuous algebraic systems, simple random multi-start plus the same refinement/checking pipeline matches or beats them.
engineering_relevance: For practical solver design, the biggest gains come from where to spend search budget and from learned repair ranking on discrete augmentations, not from replacing classical multi-start on the continuous assignment step.
method: Compare learned diffusion proposals against random multi-start under identical refinement and symbolic checking budgets.
Use a factor-graph diffusion denoiser to propose assignments, then polish with exact algebraic descent and certify with a symbolic checker.
Evaluate a candidate-conditioned repair ranker for structural augmentations against exhaustive and budget-matched baselines.
evidence_signal: The repair ranker reached near-exhaustive performance on balanced nonlinear menu selection (0.997 vs 0.236 random, p < 10^-70), while random multi-start followed the exact success curve 1-(1-q(n))^K with mean absolute error 0.012 and often matched learned proposals.
watch_item: Results depend strongly on the system regime and on sharing the same refinement/checker pipeline, so gains from learned proposals may disappear once variables are coupled or when the baseline uses enough random restarts.
paper_title: When Do Learned Diffusion Proposals Help Constraint Solving? A Controlled Study on Continuous Algebraic Systems
